statements.status_notes: CVE-2016-2781: chroot in GNU coreutils, run with --userspec, leaves the program it starts attached to the caller's terminal, so that program can push characters into the parent session's input with the TIOCSTI ioctl and have the parent shell run them. See the Debian tracker: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2016-2781 and Debian bug https://bugs.debian.org/816320 . GNU coreutils has not changed chroot for this: src/chroot.c at the v9.8 tag has no setsid() call and no TIOCSTI handling, and the Debian tracker notes that fixing it with setsid() would introduce regressions. In both published coreutils packages for Alpine 3.23, 9.8-r1 and 9.8-r2 on x86_64 and aarch64, /usr/sbin/chroot is a symlink to the multi-call /bin/coreutils binary, which carries the --userspec option and does not import setsid(): its dynamic symbol table imports chroot, setgroups and ioctl from the C library but not setsid. The mitigation is in the Linux kernel. Since Linux 6.2, TIOCSTI can be switched off with the CONFIG_LEGACY_TIOCSTI build option or the dev.tty.legacy_tiocsti sysctl: https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/torvalds/linux.git/commit/?id=83efeeeb3d04b22aaed1df99bc70a48fe9d22c4d and since Linux 6.5 processes with CAP_SYS_ADMIN can still use it when it is switched off: https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/torvalds/linux.git/commit/?id=690c8b804ad2eafbd35da5d3c95ad325ca7d5061 . The Debian tracker notes that TIOCSTI has been disabled on the kernel side since linux 6.4.4-1, a change requested in Debian bug https://bugs.debian.org/1033095 , and marks the CVE fixed in trixie from coreutils 9.4-1, the first coreutils upload after that kernel change, rather than for a coreutils change. Alpine's tracker lists coreutils 9.8-r1 in 3.23-main as possibly vulnerable: https://security.alpinelinux.org/vuln/CVE-2016-2781 . In a container, whether TIOCSTI is available depends on the host kernel and its settings, not on this package, so no property of the published coreutils builds settles it. Pending a maintainer decision on whether a host-kernel mitigation is enough to record this owner as not affected, it stays under investigation.
